Title: Speech at the opening cocktail of the 2018 edition of the Finance Summit (April 10, 2018)
text: Speech by Governor Jean Baden Dubois at the opening cocktail of the 2018 edition of the Finance Summit (April 10, 2018) Ladies and Gentlemen, Here comes the time of promising seeds. This year again, through the abundance of ideas, each more equal than the other but never short of inspiration and innovation. This year, to lead the reflection, literally and figuratively, by giving the seed of ideas the properties that will germinate the seedlings in fruitful harvests for the agricultural sector. And that's good! April is the month of our financial summit but it is also the season of seeded spaces. A finance summit to fuel the reflection around the financing of agribusiness in Haiti... This is part of a broader thematic context. He associates the reflection on the perspectives to be identified around Bitcoin but especially blockchain technology. It is therefore a clear sign that the door to innovation remains wide open. Ladies and Gentlemen, You therefore understand the immense interest that I want to share with you around this summit which, like each of the previous ones, bears the seal of a certain particularity. The particularity in this case is that it concerns what is fundamental in the chain of human production activities: the primary sector. You allow me not to spare myself to recall that in Haiti this sector revolves essentially around the agricultural branch. There are these evidences that we often like to evoke but that the brain seems to hide from our visual field or scratch from our field of action. It is not a culpable redundancy if I add that Haiti is an agricultural country. However, it is clear that this lesson passed down to more than two centuries of generations of women and men has remained rather sterile. Like a slogan without substance that would only have served to give a good conscience to our national conscience. It is against this backdrop that I want to welcome this reservoir of ideas that you represent and this renewed energy that your actions are able to sustain. I address a special greeting to the State authorities who are enhancing today's ceremony with their presence. It is an expression of interest that encourages us to believe that the considerations and proposals that will emerge from the exchanges will gradually take shape in public policy agendas. It is this perspective that justifies the warm welcome we address to the community of actors involved in the chains of activities related to the agricultural sector. I am referring to agribusiness and agribusiness investors; farmers and professionals of all stripes interested in this issue. I extend these greetings with the same emphasis to the media professionals who will give this essential leverage effect in the dissemination of the ideas that will be produced. To the rest of the audience, actors present with us or who will read the reflections through the media niches, I say to your brands because these ideas will be useless if you do not know how to translate them into entrepreneurial actions. Finally, allow me to place a well-deserved thank you to the organizers. Once again this year, the growth group and the BRH Committee pulled out all the stops. The richness of the exchanges that led to the choice of themes and that led to the establishment of the activities of the Summit testifies to this know-how that has never wavered and which now takes the form of passion. I would like CEO Kesner Pharel to find here and transmit to the Growth Group, the expression of the clear satisfaction of the Board of Directors of BRH with this fruitful partnership whose results are commensurate with the promises. I would also like to thank the BRH executives involved at one level or another in the organizing activities of this Finance Summit for the diligence and competence they put into it. The challenge, shared with your peers at Groupe Croissance, to make agribusiness financing coexist with the prospects of blockchain technology is that of intelligence and faith in the future. Ladies and Gentlemen, The question of financing the Haitian economy has always been at the heart of public policy issues. And the corollary question of the mobilization of resources for this purpose has a distant origin in the first major trade-off that politicians had to make between honoring the debt of independence and financing the development of the economic and social infrastructure of a nation fresh from an emancipatory but devastating war. This lends credence to the idea that the country's development is burdened with a very heavy initial liability. The policies inspired by the different paradigms that crossed the international economic order in the period preceding and following the Bretton Woods agreements did not lead to a lasting transformation of economic structures in Haiti. Even today, and more than in the past, we are reduced to seeing a heavy economic liability in the entire Haitian socio-economic panorama. The trend gap between an exponential demographic profile and a stagnant economic profile over the last decades broadly expresses this observation. But the most striking illustration is sectoral. It refers to the situation of the agricultural branch and that of the sectors linked to it. It is a sector that is still credited with nearly half of the employed population but which has seen its share in the country's overall output fall from more than 40% to about 25% in recent years. I will not insult the experts who will speak to you authoritatively about the problem of the sector to bring you more statistics that are now commonplace. But I will point out, with the necessary precautions, the low productivity that this drop in added value infers in the presence of such a high occupancy rate. I will go a little further by suggesting a closer confrontation of this decline with the hypothesis of a non-negative growth of the rural population through the following two considerations: If population growth compensates for the reducing effect of labour mobility and migration on the level of the rural population, the number of persons employed in the agricultural sector would be at least equal to the level it was 25 years ago. As in addition, the decline in the share of value added of the agricultural sector has occurred in a context of stagnation of overall value added and therefore of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) this implies an absolute decline in agricultural production over this period. The joint analysis of these two dynamics should therefore reinforce concerns about low productivity in the production chains if we want to ensure the financing of agribusiness in conditions of profitability that frees it from the traps of sustainable subsidy. It is in this spirit that the BRH addresses the issue of financing Agri Business in Haiti. Productivity as a leitmotif allows the development of the agricultural sector and related value chains to be viewed in a way that emphasizes the need to avoid past institutional mistakes and associated costs, reduce intermediation risks for financing institutions and make the agricultural environment more susceptible to the efficiency factors of technological innovation. Finally, it makes it easier to arrange the necessary exit routes where it is desirable for the monetary authority (the public authorities) to make sectoral incursions into the spheres of the real sector. This last aspect is of paramount importance for (the monetary authority) the central banker is forced to make a continuous trade-off between his mission of stability and the sharing of responsibilities for growth and jobs. All with tools limited in number by the very borders of financial orthodoxy that ensure its strength and credibility. In an economy of oligopolistic markets, internal and external structural imbalances like that of Haiti, the adoption of a productivity path over a reasonable horizon can temper the interventionist's criticisms of cautious postures and reason the impatience of the orthodox in the face of certain latitudes. The experience of unconventional policies conducted after the 2008 crisis in both large market and smaller economies reinforced our conviction that the boundaries of orthodoxy were not immutable. The reversal of this stance a few years later suggests that the very flexibility of these borders as a conditioning factor for monetary policy is itself arbitrated. This is why the necessary efforts to maintain macroeconomic stability in the face of the large twin deficits of the Haitian economy do not exclude the development of channels to support growth as long as the criteria of profitability and efficiency determine the sectors of intervention and their time horizon. Here are the preliminary considerations that militate in favor of a Pro-Growth Monetary Agenda. Today, the problems inherent in the agricultural sector and the sectors linked to it call for in-depth reflection if we want this broad field of activity to benefit from the facilities made possible by the provisions of our agenda under conditions that befit the new efficiency of monetary policy. The 2018 Finance Summit offers this framework for reflection. The cohabitation of the theme of financing agribusiness and that of blockchain technology opens the way to a prospective look at the search for synergy in the articulation of value chains created through secondary and tertiary primary activities that revolve around agricultural sectors. This cohabitation should also make it possible to produce reflections on the levers needed to raise productivity in the sector. I wish you a good participation and fruitful exchanges. Ladies and Gentlemen, The financing of agribusiness and the use of the technological facilities of the blockchain fit easily into the canvas of the BRH's actions built around the three axes of intervention that make it possible to give substance to its growth strategy: The development of financial markets to promote the creation of financial tools capable of mobilizing savings and increasing the financing options of the economy. It will be aligned with the national financial inclusion strategy; Financial inclusion to expand access and availability of financial products and services defined as levers in the development of economic activity. The pro-growth agenda to promote the incentive framework to direct investments towards high value-added sectors. The articulation of these axes is seen as a generating system that accommodates the sectoral particularities and technological environments that support their development. And in each case, the contours of a virtuous circle emerge thanks to the synergies transmitted by the components of this enlarged system. The idea of a balance specific to an ecosystem dynamic suits our purpose well. In the case that concerns us here, agribusiness supported by the technological facilities of the blockchain would see increase in quantity and quality the incentive signals transmitted to financial resources in search of investments generating productive value and therefore growth. All according to patterns of interrelationship within the components and between the components of the system. Here, with a touch of sophistication that I am far from looking for, is the approach around which the BRH hopes to see the reflections that will abound during these meetings. The latter represent an additional opportunity for the Central Bank to influence actions that free monetary policy from adverse conditions. These conditions, as you know, are institutional and structural in nature and they involve actions by both the private and public sectors. Their prevalence forces the Central Bank to entrench itself in a defensive attitude that resembles stabilization as an a priori posture. However, the stability sought is the result of a virtuous balance that contributes to creating wealth that only growth flows can feed in a sustainable and self-sustaining way. This is why our posture of stability is far from being the one that restricts the flow of activity. Hence the need to affirm our credo in healthy and renewed growth. This is also why our pro-growth agenda is far from being an invitation to monetary activism. Hence the need to put into practice the promotion of a stable macro-financial environment. The balance, in such a structural context, is on the razor's edge. Our approach is therefore to prevent the monetary authority from the torpor of the tightrope walker clinging to its pole, by transforming this balance into a practicable path where public policies are at ease. A key element in the success of this effort is the adoption of a forward-looking attitude that technological innovations can bear fruit. It is with this in mind that the analysis of the niches of insertion of agribusiness in the framework of interventions of the BRH and that of the catalytic role of blockchain technology in this process constitute an area of interest for reflection and action. Ladies and Gentlemen, Resource constraints have always been perceived as predominant in the implementation of development policies in Haiti. However, this assertion is not exclusive of the problem of the adequacy of public policies and the broader problem of a holistic approach that can weigh and interlink the multiple dimensions of the development problem. That is why economic development assistance, despite its usefulness, is limited in scope because it does not create an intergenerational process of wealth creation. It is therefore understandable why the effort to deepen and broaden the existing financial system constitutes the basis for a broader objective of developing financial markets that is concomitant with that of the growth sectors of the economy. The implementation of the National System of Financial Inclusion is there to give socio-economic weight to this approach. And it is this broad financial device that should benefit the financing of agribusiness while benefiting. Because it is a question of giving the strategic state the means to promote the entire economic system according to an approach that joins all its multiple components. I am therefore pleased to see a process of diversification of financial products that allows: To finance the cash flow needs of the various chains of agribusiness activities To finance the capitalization of agricultural and agro-industrial companies through capital investments and securitization of long-term debt To introduce public titles for the financing of infrastructure in the agricultural sector. At the same time, the added value generated in agribusiness should strengthen the income distributed in the agricultural and agro-industrial sectors through better remuneration for the factors employed. The transmission of managed value doesn't stop there. It is expected to fuel demand for financial products and spur innovation in deeper financial markets through, inter alia: The creation of a secondary market for public and private financial securities The development of reinsurance for companies in the sector A better assessment and mitigation of risks that will allow a broader customer base and transactions between companies in the sector and the financial system. The institutional environment that will serve as a link to this incubation process is gradually being put in place. The financing facilities that BRH makes available to the agricultural and agro-industrial sectors through banking intermediation already represent a first achievement. More broadly, the BRH has undertaken a series of initiatives that should gradually weave new networks of interaction between the actors concerned. Among the most important are: Support for agricultural insurance programs; Strengthening credit unions in rural areas; The creation of sectoral tables around different agricultural sectors; Increased consultations with the budgetary and tax authorities with a view to developing a market for government securities; The establishment of legislation allowing the creation of financial institutions authorized to issue securities on behalf of private companies. Ladies and Gentlemen, Our reflections would not think outside the box if they did not combine them with the important factor of technological innovation. The development of financing instruments will not be able to help strengthen links in the value chain and increase the value added of the sector if the improvement in factor productivity is not achieved in both the real and financial spheres of production of goods and services related to the sector. Two preliminary considerations hold my attention. At the current stage of its development, what is the potential for exploiting this technology for the benefit of the sector? How can we avoid sinking into sterile conjecture about the virtues of blockchain and discrediting our approach by exposing ourselves to the risks of a technology whose opinions on the use we make of it in the financial field are still widely shared? At the outset, I would say that we are sufficiently equipped as a central banker to anticipate and manage these risks without reducing our forward-looking view of the potential for exploiting this technology. Let's give ourselves a sufficiently simple understanding of this technology to facilitate reflection on the place reserved for it in the ecosystem mentioned above. Blockchain is a virtually unlimited domain of highly secure ledgers of information of various natures with the degree of detail befitting the transparency needs of a specific activity. Its use can therefore be of immediate scope by helping to alleviate many institutional constraints or to deepen certain bottlenecks that hinder the creation of productive value and often prohibitive transaction costs for the investor. The example that comes to mind in the field of agricultural production is the ease of use of this technology in terms of traceability and product certification. A possibility of great interest as part of a strategy for the development of organic export agriculture. This facility can provide the livestock sectors with the same leverage effects. The use of blockchain technology may also be structural in scope. In this light, it is full of promise for areas as diverse as the identification of land titles, which is central to any efficient process of modernization of the agricultural sector, especially in relation to the problem of financing that weighs on it. It has the qualities of an important technological shortcut that improves productivity in fields that cover a wide time horizon of activities. Financial products that could be used to finance value chains linked to agricultural production are largely part of this. And fortunately. Because in an institutional context where banking intermediation is predominant if not exclusive, blockchain creates for agri business the prospect of direct financing within the framework of investment schemes often discouraged by conventional banks subject to more stringent prudential standards. Here are the following diagrams: Fundraising through Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs). This is... ) a process that is cheaper, more accessible and faster than mobilizing resources through bank financing or venture capital funds; The creation of insurance and risk coverage products through contracts whose honesty is guaranteed by the real-time computer verification of their execution process. These so-called smart contracts can thus be used to ensure the execution of index insurance contracts in the agricultural sector, particularly because of their low cost and their lower vulnerability to fraud. Facilitating remittances by reducing transaction costs. The very nature of the BlockChain makes it a technology applicable in almost all fields of activity. And the controversies it arouses can prove beneficial for a rapid development of its potentials within the framework of a standardized use. It is desirable that national institutions that have sufficient means and adequate skills in information technology take a closer interest in blockchain. The BRH is already in standby mode in the domain. The aim is to build the capacity to efficiently exploit the opportunities it offers while avoiding the pitfalls of deviant use and the undue costs associated with fraud. On a broader basis, it is a question of making the economy benefit from the virtues of this technology within the framework of a proactive and strategic attitude and not passive as was the case with the Internet in the mid-90s. If the effects induced by this technology are up to expectations, "entire sectors of the economy in fields as diverse as finance, IT, logistics or agriculture are expected to be affected by this technology with opportunities for job creation, new fields of business and business opportunities. From this point of view, blockchain is a technological tool full of promise for the development of economic activities. As such, this innovation can play an important role in the BRH's pro-growth agenda and is likely to put a new technological tool at the service of wealth creation in a sustainable and equitable way. So let's keep our feet on the ground by methodically scanning the technological horizon. Ladies and Gentlemen, A speech cannot go around the problem of financing agribusiness in Haiti. A field of intersectoral activities that revolves around the sector strategically and socially most important for the country: agriculture. I would be careful not to develop enough certain aspects of the ecosystem idea that we want to promote if I did not have the certainty of their development in the in-depth discussions that will take place over the next few days of the sessions. Some aspects that have to do with the interrelations between agribusiness financing and our monetary agenda for growth must be rigorously analyzed if we want to make the financing scheme we propose a pilot experiment. The idea of ecosystem fits well with our purpose. It accurately configures the angle of view that we want to see crossed in the development action of the sector where this notion finds its fullest expression. I would suggest the need to discuss the controversies caused by the proliferation of activities that revolve around the blockchain. It would only be a pavement in the pond if I were not committed to the idea, that in terms of ideas, the best comfort comes from confrontation. These controversies therefore come at the right time in this phase of maturation of this technology. They ensure greater sustainability if it holds up to expectations. Ladies and Gentlemen, So here we go for the collection of ideas. My speech began my speech rather saw in these foundations a space for the seed of ideas. Powerful nature that makes the hen the egg she lays. Also from seed to collection there is the matrix space of maturation. The Finance Summit has become this space for the maturation of ideas. And he sows to all winds to borrow this image of the little Larousse of the years of yesteryear. I therefore invite you to toast to the success of this conference. Because the best vintage is drunk at the time of the great harvests. May this week's reflections lead us into the era of successful harvests for the agricultural sector. I would like to express the wish of each of the many participants in this 8th edition of the Finance Summit. And this is also my most precious wish. Thank you!

text: Speech by Governor Jean Baden Dubois on the occasion of the launch of Audit Week (12 November 2018) Ladies and Gentlemen, Mr. Chairman of the Board of Directors of IAI-Haiti Presidents of Commercial Banks and Financial Institutions Mr. Coordinator of the Economic Forum Mr. Outgoing President of UFAI Ladies & Gentlemen Representatives of the spoken, written and televised press Ladies and gentlemen. As you can see it's huge! These two indicators alone show the magnitude of the problem we face. In this sense, the fight against corruption and money-laundering is at the centre of efforts to stabilize, modernize and expand the country's financial system. Therefore, no effort is being spared by BRH to ensure that Haiti adopts and applies as effectively as possible all the provisions for the prevention, detection and investigation of money-laundering in its area of competence. Among these initiatives, we can highlight the fact that, since 2008, through several circulars relating to regulatory oversight (for example, Circular #95-1), the BRH requires all financial institutions under its supervision to obtain from its customers a declaration of the source of funds above a threshold of 400 thousand gourdes. The regulatory framework also requires these financial institutions to set up a compliance department responsible for managing compliance with regulatory provisions in general and the provisions on money laundering in particular, including the responsibility to report suspicious transactions to UCREF whenever they deem it necessary. The BRH ensures through regular inspections of financial institutions that all these provisions are respected. Also, as an active member of the National Committee for the Fight against Asset Laundering (CNLBA), the governance body of UCREF, the BRH plays a direct role in the strategic management of the national policy on money laundering. At the same time, BRH is at the forefront of efforts to ensure Haiti's compliance with these commitments to the Caribbean Financial Action Task Force (CFATF), particularly with regard to the adoption of legislation. We recall the conference of August 26, 2016 where the BRH, together with the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, brought together all national actors to adapt the legal mechanisms for the prevention, detection and suppression of money laundering and terrorist financing. Other examples include awareness-raising sessions for journalists on the issue of money laundering. The list of initiatives is long and I will focus on the most recent and significant ones. With regard to the fight against corruption, and the promotion of good governance, the BRH acts both internally and at the level of regulated institutions. Internally since 1995 the central bank has set up an independent internal audit function which, among other tasks, is responsible for the prevention, detection and investigation of fraud. This function was strengthened in 2007 by reporting to the Audit Committee composed of a majority of external members. In addition, in terms of procurement, the BRH has established within it a Specialized Commission for Public Procurement (CSMP) responsible for organizing the award of all contracts above the threshold set by law and which must be the subject of upstream and downstream authorization by the National Commission for Public Procurement (CNMP). In order to guarantee its independence, no member of the Board of Directors or of the Bank's senior management (Governor, Deputy Governor, Managing Director) may be part of the CSMP. In order to strengthen the capacities of the latter, BRH executives receive specialized training ranging from local and international seminars to obtaining the certification of Manager Specialist in Public Procurement (MSMP) issued by the World Bank. Of the four MSMP in Haiti, BRH has half. Still in terms of anti-corruption action, since 1998 (Circular 89), commercial banks have been obliged to set up an internal audit function. This initiative has contributed not only to the improvement of the governance of financial institutions but also to the emergence of this community of specialists who now form IAI-HAiTI. The central bank is therefore proud to be at the base of the establishment of this profession in Haiti and, by extension, to have contributed to the fight against corruption. To sum up, in terms of good governance, transparency and the prevention of corruption, we can say without pretension that the BRH and supervised financial institutions can serve as a model for the public sector as well as for the rest of the Haitian private sector. And this is particularly true in the current situation. In this regard, we must pay great tribute to the regulated institutions in general and particularly to the banks that tirelessly demonstrate their commitment to good governance and respect for the law on a daily basis. This is evidenced by the fact that of the 20 largest Haitian taxpayers 4 are commercial banks (it should be noted that the 21st largest taxpayer is also a bank and a state bank to boot!). By their example, these financial intermediaries prove that it is possible to be profitable, even very profitable while respecting the law and observing good governance in Haiti. As for the financing of terrorism, make no mistake. It is a scourge to which all countries are exposed. Whether they are direct victims or not, States have a moral duty to play their part so that their territory and financial system are not used for this purpose. In a world that tends towards polarization and inward-looking, the use of violence and terrorism may unfortunately be the choice of some. It is up to us to be vigilant so as not to be complicit in their actions either through inaction or lack of rigour. Let us be aware of this and let us remain vigilant. The BRH, for its part, will continue to do everything in its power to fully play its role and cooperate with all jurisdictions when called upon and ensure that Haiti is not a weak link in the international financial system. It should be strongly emphasized that resistance to these scourges cannot be led solely by the financial sector; An independent, effective and efficient judicial system, with human, technical, financial and material resources, is a necessary condition for the success of this fight against financial crimes. To this end, the BRH stands ready to do everything it can within the limits of its legal attributions, through the CNLBA and any other initiatives or measures taken by the authorities and our international partners. It is then up to us to arm ourselves with courage and determination in order to continue this struggle. With that, ladies and gentlemen, I wish you a good audit week and an excellent evening. See you next year! Thank you! Port-au-Prince, 12 November 2018

text: Opening speech delivered by Governor Jean Baden Dubois on the occasion of the presentation "Credit Rating: A Modern Tool in Risk Management" hosted by FICO and Turbo System. Opening speech by Governor Jean Baden Dubois on the occasion of the presentation "Credit Rating: A Modern Tool in Risk Management" hosted by FICO and Turbo System. Thursday, January 25, 2018 Dear Colleagues of the Board of Directors, Ladies and Gentlemen Chief Executive Officers of Financial Institutions Mr. Director of Turbo System, Dear Collaborators, Dear Guests Ladies / Gentlemen After decades in the development of computer systems and information technology, as in the national financial universe, both in the private sector and at BRH, it gives me particular pleasure to introduce the Credit Information Bureau, our BIC, to this new stage of its expansion for the benefit of a healthy and sustainable growth of the economy through the distribution of credit. In December 2013, I had the great honour, as Director General of the BRH, to preside over the launch ceremony of the first data submission tests with local banks. In four years, the BIC has come a long way, having gained the confidence of financial intermediaries and also a strategic place in the future development of the payments system and, consequently, the economy. Let me briefly remind you that the main mission of the Bureau d'Information sur le Credit, initiated by the Bank of the Republic of Haiti in 1999, is to operate a system of information on the credit history of economic agents in the Haitian financial system. The idea of setting up the first Credit Bureau is intended to promote the sharing of credit information and thus allow the various financial institutions to have a better approach to the granting of credit. The objectives of this new agency are inspired by the general policy and long-term action of the BRH Board of Directors, which wants to tackle the major challenge of democratizing credit while limiting risks. The BIC is also called upon to play a major role in the central bank's financial inclusion policy, together with other public authorities. Ladies and Gentlemen, I was telling you that the Bureau of Credit Information has grown. The number of credit reports solicited (by credit providers) increased from 5683 in July 2017 (start of operations) to 12333 four months later (in December), reaching 62096 to date. Such dynamism reflects the intensity of the credit market as well as the importance of information for risk management and, consequently, the growing importance of the BIC. In the medium and long term, institutions such as the Bureau d'Information sur le Credit (BIC), the Industrial Development Fund (FDI), are called upon to play extremely important strategic roles in the economy and the BRH is ready to make every effort to enable them to face the challenges that may affect their performance. For the BIC specifically, we anticipate a continuous improvement of their database as well as the incorporation of certain functions of the former Risk Central. It is also planned to integrate three non-bank financial institutions, FDI, Sohfides and Ayiti Leasing, and to start a pilot project for the admission of savings banks. The BIC will also develop new products for the financial system, i.e. new credit reports such as credit scoring or credit scoring, a tool, allowing a numerical assessment of the potential risk of lending to a client, which will facilitate the making of loan granting decisions in a timely and fair manner. This product will be developed with FICO, the world leader in analytical software, thanks to a technical partnership with Turbo System. At this stage of the debates, as the credit scoring project is the subject of our meeting this morning, I give the floor to Mr Darbouze of Turbo System. Thank you! Title: Speech on the occasion of the transfer of funds from SYFAAH to the IDF
text: Governor's speech on the occasion of the transfer of funds from SYFAAH to the IDF The Minister of Agriculture; The Officer-in-Charge of Canada's Canadian Cooperation in Haiti; The Ambassador of Switzerland to Haiti; Members of the BRH Council; The Director-General of the IDF; The Director-General of the ACO; Mr. Director of the SYFAAH Project; Ladies and gentlemen executives of the MEF, the BRH and the FDI; Distinguished guests, It is with great satisfaction that I participate in this ceremony which will consecrate the transfer of funds from the SYFAAH project, which expires on March 31, 2019, to the Industrial Development Fund (IDF). The BRH, from the beginning, has always worked in synergy with the Ministry of Agriculture, SYFAAH and other institutional actors, in the establishment of the ecosystem required for the development of agricultural financing in Haiti. It is committed to remaining proactive in the process, playing a central role in consolidating the mechanisms developed with the support of SYFAAH. These focused respectively on financing, risk mitigation tools via ASREC and partial credit guarantees (FAPAAH). We will therefore strive to perpetuate these achievements with a view to establishing, in a structuring way, a reliable institutional environment to support the financing of agriculture. To substantially impact the expanded access to credit in the country, this framework will have to provide as a prerequisite, the marketing of crop insurance. This instrument has been tested through a pilot phase of the project, for the rice sector, in the Artibonite department. It has produced convincing results. The risk coverage it offered prompted financial institutions to expand access to credit for small producers. The result was a WIN-WIN, both for financial institutions and debtors. The latter, when natural hazards materialized, causing significant material losses, received compensation that allowed them to go back into business and restructure their loans. At the same time, creditor institutions were assured that their resources would not be adversely affected by their decisions to extend credit to this category of debtors deemed vulnerable. The commercialization of crop insurance implies as a prerequisite the establishment of a reserve fund, to compensate for the lack of agricultural reinsurance coverage in Haiti. This fund will help to enable Credit Agricole's portfolio to reach a critical size sufficient to whet the appetite of agricultural reinsurers for the Haitian market. The BRH, as a facilitator at the Ministry of Agriculture, has always worked in the supervision and stimulation of the agricultural sector with a view to: Identify promising sectors connected to viable markets through the financing of studies; To facilitate synergies between actors operating in value chains through the organization of sectoral consultation tables around promising sectors; Increase financing through the introduction of financial incentive mechanisms focusing mainly on the exemption of minimum reserves (circular 108), the granting of cash advances to financial institutions at very low rates (circular 113). These incentives target producers and exporters of agricultural products. They are adapted to the short, medium and long-term needs of the sector; BRH aims to see the IDF play a leading role in the expansion of agricultural and agro-industrial financing across the country. In this context, it welcomes the transfer of the remaining SYFAAH funds and the transfers of powers carried out in recent months. I would like to take this opportunity to commend the efforts of the management team, in particular Mr. Jeudy, to improve the governance of the institution. The BRH will accompany the IDF in its reinforcement. In the light of recent evaluation reports carried out respectively by SYFAAH, the IDB and the Frankfurt Institute, the latter mandated by the European Investment Bank (EIB), we have already begun the process of supporting improved governance of the IDF, in particular through: On-site and documentary supervision of the IDF, as well as the other institutions we regulate; The permanent assignment of an executive from our Internal Audit Unit to the FDI; Ad hoc support focused on the provision of specific technical support, particularly in the budget preparation and control processes; By letter dated March 20, addressed to DID Desjardins, the BRH confirmed its commitment to support the institutional environment required for improved agricultural financing. At the same time, she highlighted the financial contributions of the State, to ASREC and FAPAAH, of 80 million gourdes in 2017-18. This amount represents the dividends that the BRH pays to the Ministry of Economy and Finance, every year according to a legal obligation. She also mentioned the financial support it provides to the sector through financial institutions. This commitment concerns a ceiling amount of 5 billion gourdes per year. I will conclude by thanking Canada, DID Desjardins, all the staff of the SYFAAH project, in particular, its director, Mr. Charland, the Swiss Cooperation for their contributions to the genesis of an embryonic ecosystem of agricultural financing and coverage of associated risks in Haiti. We will work to ensure that this initiative is sustainable and that it extends throughout the country and extends to all the country's promising sectors. We encourage both the central government and bilateral and multilateral donors to finance or increase their financing for crop insurance and partial credit guarantees. In this way, agriculture will be able to play its role as an engine of sustained and sustainable economic growth, with impacts on: The lower inflation and macroeconomic stability in general; Some significant foreign exchange earnings from agricultural exports; Increasing incomes in rural areas; Some massive job creation; One significant reduction of poverty and expansion of the middle class; The reducing the economy's vulnerabilities to external shocks; Some positive impact on cross-cutting sectors such as tourism. Thank you for your attention Port-au-Prince, 27 March 2019

Title: Remarks on the occasion of the signature sale of the books of the Central Bank's 40th Anniversary Collection
text: Remarks on the occasion of Mr. Jean Baden Dubois, Governor of the BRH, on the occasion of the signature sale of the books of the Collection of the 40th anniversary of the Central Bank Remarks by Mr. Jean Baden Dubois, Governor of the BRH, on the occasion of the signature sale of the books of the Central Bank's 40th Anniversary Collection Ladies and Gentlemen, Members of the Government, Ladies and Gentlemen, Members of the Board of Directors of the BRH, Ladies and Gentlemen, Members of the Diplomatic Corps and International Institutions, Ladies and Gentlemen, Representatives of Financial Institutions and Partners of the BRH, Ladies and Gentlemen, Representatives of Civil Society Organizations, Academic Institutions and Cultural Organizations, Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, On behalf of the Board of Directors that I have the honour to chair, I would like to begin by thanking you for having responded positively to our invitation on the occasion of this event, which is part of the activities commemorating the 40th anniversary of the creation of the Bank of the Republic of Haiti. I would also like to thank the authors and publishers who have worked so hard to produce and print the books that are now the subject of this signature sale. In particular, I would like to express my respect and admiration for the work accomplished, in sometimes difficult conditions, by the authors whose work we are celebrating today, I quote Guerdy Lissade, Daniel Supplice, Jean-Herold Perard, Max etienne, and all the writers who collaborated under the direction of the historian Pierre Buteau in the production of the book "The South in the diversity of its heritage". In the same token of thanks, I join in thanking the men and women of culture who have already contributed to enriching our collections within the framework of close cooperation with the numismatic museum of the BRH, either by joint production or by the republication of little-known works. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Tonight's meeting is an event that should be well situated in relation to the spirit that gave birth to it. As I mentioned earlier, our meeting is part of the panoply of cultural activities planned to mark the 40th anniversary of the BRH. But, beyond this aspect, it reflects above all the desire of the Central Bank to inscribe its patronage and its cultural programming in the direction of a preferential interest in works that correspond to its mission and its history. I am particularly inspired by the tone and content of the 32nd "Tacitus Lecture" that Christine Lagarde, Managing Director of the IMF, gave in London on February 28, in which she urges international finance to redefine a "financial sector that looks beyond its raison d'etre". It is this type of discourse that feeds the action of the Council over which I preside and which motivates the trade-off we make between the central banker's demand for rigour and the public servant's obligation to be open to the social whole. Our action in this area is based on simple and universally established principles, which can be listed as follows: Favour the development of the cultural heritage of the Haitian State; Preserve this heritage and to provide access to it to the widest possible public for the purposes of education and edification; Of More specifically, to use this heritage to promote financial education and basic knowledge of economics. On the first point, that relating to the development of the cultural heritage of the Haitian State, the BRH already has an important historical and artistic fund that houses a whole collection of paintings as well as other original works of art. It also holds a numismatic collection that it strives to enrich. In addition, we remember that in 2014 we put into circulation a selection of books that were an integral part of the BRH's 35th anniversary collection. Among these books were those of Frederic Marcelin, Antenor Firmin, Vilfort Beauvoir, Raymond Renaud and Joseph Chatelain. Each of these books evokes important moments in our history as reflected through the evolution of our currency, our institutions and our economic relations with our partners. On June 10, 2017, the BRH proceeded to the signature sale of the book "Haiti through its currency", produced under the direction of the writer Michel Soukar. It was a formidable research work presenting the testimonies of actors who had marked centuries of Haitian monetary history, from Moreau de Saint-Mery to Claude Moise, via Perceval Thoby and John Spencer. On April 6, 2018, it was the turn of "The Treasures of the Republic", a work resulting from the partnership between the BRH and the National Pantheon Museum. This book is the result of a combination judicious collections of MUPANAH and the BRH Numismatic Museum. Let us now come to the 2nd principle that inspires the patronage and cultural programming of the Central Bank of Haiti. This is the principle of preservation and popularization of the cultural heritage of the Haitian State. The severe damage caused by the earthquake of 12 January 2010 included damage to important cultural objects. Without delay, the BRH embarked on a restoration campaign that benefited from the technical assistance of the France. Many paintings could be repaired, including "The Oath of the Ancestors". With regard to the 3rd principle  economic and financial education  apart from open days, we take advantage of every important event to invite schools to participate in our activities. Thus, although the BRH Numismatic Museum is not yet fully open to the public, several schools have had the opportunity to visit the exhibition hall. These visits provided an opportunity for the BRH to organize workshops for young people on the history of money and the missions of the BRH. Ultimately, our ambition is to promote economic and financial education through the establishment of a museum space dedicated to the interaction of the BRH with schoolchildren and academics. That, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, is how far we have already come in terms of enriching our collections. And that brings us to the subject of tonight's meeting: the BRH's 40th anniversary book collection. I know the authors will be giving a fuller presentation on signature books, but let me say a few words about it. Let's start with the book designed under the direction of historian Pierre Buteau, and entitled "The South in the diversity of its heritage". This book highlights the part of Afro-Latin wandering and the importance of the principle of reciprocity in the fierce struggle for freedom in Latin America, a few years after Haiti's independence. And, beyond Simon Bolivar's visit to the South of our country, it recalls the promise made by the Libertador to President Alexandre Petion to abolish slavery wherever he has triumphed. In addition, fauna, flora, festivities, socio-political movements are present in this work, not to mention cuisine, music and painters from the South. So many elements find a special place in this beautiful celebration of the greatness, diversity and pride of this region of the country. Guerdy Lissade's book, "Les billets de banque de la Republique d'Haiti", tells us, through currency, the difficult transition from the colonial system to the sovereignty of the Haitian State that emerged from it. From the cash note to the paper money, the story takes us into the meanders of the monetary history of a state bruised and divided after the death of Jean-Jacques Dessalines. From the Revolution of 1843 to the Second Empire of Soulouque, to the Restoration of 1859, then to the Paper Triumvirate and the time of reforms, this book allows us to understand the historical journey that, in 1915, led to the American occupation. In this box of three pieces, it is the entire culture of Haitian currency that is in the spotlight. You are all invited to travel in the world of money, with first-hand information and very well illustrated pages. As for Daniel Supplice's book, "Haiti  History and Constitutions", it has the interest of offering the reader abundant documentation on Haitian Constitutions for the period from July 8, 1801 to May 9, 2011. It is a historical document that the author offers us, a guide to list all the Constitutions of the Republic of Haiti. This work can only strengthen Haiti's documentary heritage. For his part, Jean-Herold Perard invites us to take a tour in the life, history and work of Henry 1st in his book: "Henry Christophe  A great unknown". This is the most recent reference book on the subject, and I have no doubt that it will contribute to the commemoration, in 2020, of the bicentenary of the death of the great King Builder. What are the most relevant political lessons, truths and information to discover about Henry Christophe? This book is more an interrogation of the man who bequeathed us the most imposing sites of Haiti's built heritage, than a judgment on a king who is often portrayed as a "progressive dictator". Finally, Max etienne's book, entitled "Monetary and Financial Code", is a new edition that many financial and legal professionals have an interest in consulting. They will find all the information they need to navigate the day-to-day business and can use it as a working tool to immerse themselves in the legislative and regulatory framework of our financial system. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Your presence here this evening testifies to your interest in history, the economy, and also in the cultural richness of our country. The BRH is proud to be able to satisfy your intellectual curiosity by organizing the sale-signature of these books that will be part of the country's literary heritage, and in the national documentation on numismatic art and science. This event is a testimony to the cultural and educational commitment of the BRH. Because, apart from the 40th anniversary collection, it is a project to disseminate culture based on the need to educate our fellow citizens about the history of our currency, this great school that enlightens them on our contradictions, our strengths and our weaknesses. I invite you to rediscover the history of Haiti through its currency, through the rules of its financial system, through its kings, its constitutions and the southern region by obtaining these books that will offer you the opportunity to help a young compatriot to learn and cultivate himself. By acquiring these books for yourself or giving them to a loved one, you will create a new opportunity for intellectual enrichment. You will be able to get closer to a person you love and contribute at the same time to the promotion of a literary, artistic, historical, sociological, scientific and numismatic work. As emile Zola said so well: "There are never too many books! We need it, and again, and always! It is by the book and not by the sword that humanity will overcome lies and injustice, will conquer the final peace of brotherhood among peoples!  I wish you a good evening and, of course, happy reading!

Title: Remarks at the Haiti Constituency Meeting at the IMF held on Friday, April 13, 2019 as part of the Spring Meetings
text: Bank of the Republic of Haiti 1. BRH 2. Governor's remarks at the Haiti constituency meeting at the IMFheld on Friday, April 13, 2019 as part of the Spring Meetings Governor's Remarks at the Haiti Constituency Meeting at the IMF held on Friday, April 13, 2019 as part of the Spring Meetings Thank you for this opportunity to share with our colleagues in the chair some information on developments in Haiti. I know that you have no doubt followed our recent challenges with interest. As you may know, at the beginning of March we reached an "ad referendum" agreement with the IMF for support under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) which should cover the next three years. Our goal with this program is to accelerate as much as possible our efforts to get out of fragility. Thus,the programme on which we have agreed attempts to strike the right balance between addressing social concerns, or better,preventing the deterioration of the social situation and taking a series of measures to ensure economic stability. Fiscal consolidation and strengthening safety nets are at the heart of the programme. It also addresses governance issues in the electricity sector, and generally contains measures to increase transparency and fight corruption. In fact, we had taken steps long before the IMF came to ensure macroeconomic stability. One of these measures is cash management, which is an agreement signed between the Bank of the Republic of Haiti and the Ministry of Economy and Finance to limit tax dominance. With this agreement, fiscal compliance should be ensured. The change of Prime Minister after the conclusion of negotiations with the IMF on the ECF will still delay the approval of the arrangement (ECF). Despite the will of the Executive and the assurances of the Legislature to move quickly with the process, the agreement with the IMF cannot be signed before the formal formation of the new Government. This is necessary not only to strengthen the IMF but also to enable us to meet the preconditions for approval of the ECF by the IMF Board. The tabling of the budget for the current fiscal year in Parliament is one of these preconditions. Under the ECF, we will need IMF support of up to 100% of our IMF quota, or about 229 million with two disbursements in the current fiscal year. The European Union and the IDB are awaiting the IMF's signal to also grant budget support totalling around USD 75 million. This support is essential for the implementation of social programmes designed to mitigate the potentially negative impact of the programme's structural measures on the most vulnerable sections of the population. As the measures included in the ECF are part of the Government's program, we continue to implement it, although the agreement with the IMF has not yet been formalized. We also believe that this should allow for no carry-over in the two planned disbursements before the end of the financial year, i.e. before the end of September 2019. I cannot conclude without thanking on behalf of the Minister and on my own behalf, the Administrator. Mr. Tombini and his DeputyMr. Saraiva (Bruno) who have been personally involved to reach this stage of concluding an agreement under the Extended Credit Facility that we have been looking for for almost two years. November 15, 2022

La consolidation fiscale etle renforcement des filets de scurit sont au cur du programme. Il adresse aussi des questions de gouvernance dans le secteur lectrique, et dune manire gnrale contientdes mesures pour accrotre la transparence et combattre la corruption. En fait, nous avions pris des mesures bien avant la venue du FMI pour assurer la stabilit macroconomique. Lune de ces mesures est le cash managementqui est un accord sign entre la Banque de la Rpublique dHati etle Ministre de lEconomie et des Finances pour limiter la dominance fiscale. Avec cet accord,la discipline fiscale devrait tre assure. Le changementde Premier Ministre aprs la clture des ngociations avec le FMI sur la FEC va tout de mme reporter lapprobation de laccord (FEC). Cela est ncessaire non seulement pour conforter le FMI mais aussi pour nous permettre de remplir les conditions pralables lapprobation de la FEC par le Conseil du FMI. Le dpt du budgetde lexercice en cours au Parlement est une de ces conditions pralables. Ces appuis sont indispensables pour implmenter les programmes sociaux devant mitiger limpactpotentiellement ngatifdes mesures structurelles du programme sur les couches les plus vulnrables de la population. Comme les mesures incluses dans la FEC fontpartie du programme du Gouvernement, nous continuons la mettre en uvre,bien que laccord ne soit pas encore officialis avec le FMI. Title: Speech by Doctor Jean Elie Larrieux Representative of Corpuha: FRD-BRH scientific days
text: Research... MENU BRH / Speech by Doctor Jean Elie Larrieux Representative of Corpuha: Scientific Days of the FRD-BRH Speech by Dr. Jean Elie Larrieux Representative of Corpuha: Scientific Days of the FRD-BRH Mr. Governor of the BRH Mr. Vice-Governor, Mr. Director General Mr. Rectors of the Universities, Ladies and gentlemen of the Press, distinguished guests, I thank the Governor, the Vice-Governor, the Director General and the organizers of this scientific meeting for having associated the university community, CORPUHA. I will quickly tell you that CORPUHA is the Conference of Rectors, Presidents of Universities and Heads of Haitian Higher Education Institutions. It brings together public and non-public higher education institutions. It has legal personality by presidential decree dated December 17, 2017. It is a non-profit organization whose fundamental mission is to promote the higher education, scientific research and technological innovation sector. For the year 2023-2024, it intends to encourage member institutions to create research laboratories and to pool their efforts in this regard. It is working to set up an intra- and inter-university doctoral training system. It is a large-scale project in the works. CORPUHA expects its projects to be actively supported by important partners such as the BRH, the AUF and other institutions. CORPUHA, through my organ, is delighted to participate in this meeting. They aim to raise awareness of the activities of the BRH Fund as a forum for academics and researchers and to solicit the attention of political decision-makers as to the benefits of organized research in terms of in-depth questioning of the Nation's problems and documented responses likely to feed the formulation of enlightened public policies. The business sector should be able to find a certain interest in it with regard to the burning concerns of national and international competition, linked to the needs of structural, promotional, market and technological innovation in the world modulated by the knowledge economy, the knowledge economy. It seems to me that the creation of this Fund and this first edition of 2 scientific days meet this need, quite well understood by the number of projects submitted, that the systematically organized production and dissemination of scholarly knowledge, techniques and technologies are essential in this 21st century. And, consequently, the academic world, the privileged melting pot of knowledge production, should be a partner pampered and supported by the State, by enlightened donors and by the business sector, if the latter wishes to participate in the changes for a new and prosperous Haiti. To overcome endemic, uncreative, uninnovative subcontracting, to create national wealth, create jobs, support young entrepreneurs, to free themselves from food and pharmaceutical tutelage, to feed the population healthily for a health system of dignity for all, and today to re-establish the State, the public power, to ensure the security of lives and property, to recreate social ties through a healthy distribution of justice and through an institutionalized practice of social and community mediation, likely to restore trust and facilitate citizen coexistence... For all these reasons, it is important to support the efforts of researchers, to support development in universities. Support for university research and development could be declined upstream and downstream, i.e. by supporting the training of new and young researchers, capable of feeding the scientific staff of universities, and, through a multiplier effect, permanently ensuring a quality scientific and academic succession. The aim is to support doctoral and post-doctoral programmes in the country, and even certain research master's degrees. At the same time, it would be a question of addressing the second aspect by encouraging the development of research through funding granted to projects according to targeted themes of general interest, addressed to all research sectors combined. This is the case of the BRH Fund. It is an interesting step towards seniors, even if young people in training can find something to learn about, but not necessarily for the purpose of academic accomplishment as researchers. It is also true that the BRH is already participating with the AUF in supporting certain doctoral students. We cannot ask the BRH for everything, but through the respectability of its status and its innovative initiatives, the BRH can validly encourage partners to help Haitian universities to train, for the most part, on the spot, the researchers that the country needs. But it is also necessary to remain attentive to all forms of international cooperation by ensuring that the structural academic strengthening of our young universities is encouraged. The concerns, needs, sensitivities and knowledge of the South are sometimes underpinned by the ideologized views of the North/South relationship of certain partners that tend to make institutions of the South invisible and to lead them to lock themselves into epistemological formalizations that would hardly promote a plural expression of knowledge, know-how and cultures. Recently, the attitudes and choices that are gratifying for health, in the face of the Covid 19 pandemic, of certain populations in the South, clearly show the interest that should be given to a plural expression of science as a mode of appropriation, codification, modeling and renewed transposition of knowledge and know-how. In this sense, in a current world in the midst of changes in traditional, economic, political, strategic and technological polarizations, it is necessary to question the epistemologies of the South as a way of opening up and strengthening Science. I therefore invite you to be open, to create, to innovate. The work of strengthening university research in Haiti, ladies and gentlemen, is complex and arduous. However, I think the milestone set by the BRH is encouraging, and others will probably follow. In conclusion, the key word is that of Max Weber: "How to be up to the task of everyday life?" And, Alfred Schutz said in the researcher and the daily newspaper (1997, 2008) "The world of everyday life is the stage and the object of our actions and interactions, we must dominate it (know it) and transform it in order to achieve the goals we pursue". Let's get to work here and now. Congratulations to the BRH, congratulations to the researchers who presented a project that was accepted or not. Have a good day's work. Thank you for your attention. Speech by Dr. Jean Elie Larrieux, University Professor Representative of the Conference of Rectors (CORPUHA) Rector of IUSE-CREFI Member of the Advisory Committee of the BRH Fund for Research and Development Port-au-Prince, May 26, 2023.
